test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A truck travels 80 km at the speed of 40 km/hr and the next 44 km at the speed of 9 km/hr. What is its average speed (in km/hr)?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = **Total Distance** ÷ **Total Time**

Total Distance = 80 + 44 = 124 km

Total Time = (80 ÷ 40) + (44 ÷ 9) = 2 + 4.888 = 6.888 hours

Average Speed = 124 ÷ (62/9) = 124 × (9/62) = 2 × 9 = 18 kmph

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Distance 1** (d₁) = 80 km, **Speed 1** (s₁) = 40 km/hr

**Distance 2** (d₂) = 44 km, **Speed 2** (s₂) = 9 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = (d₁ + d₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bfd1699f626638dfdf7248381be4c452862a752f9023e7d9a6b343ce65845e4.png] 

⇒ Time taken for first part (t₁) = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken for second part (t₂) = 44 ÷ 9 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 80 + 44 = 124 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 44/9 = (18 + 44) ÷ 9 = 62/9 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 124 ÷ (62/9)

⇒ Average Speed = 124 × 9 ÷ 62 = 2 × 9 = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds u and v, the average speed is 2uv ÷ (u + v).

General Average Speed Formula

Average speed is always the total distance divided by the total time taken, regardless of speed variations.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is s₁ − s₂. In opposite directions, it is s₁ + s₂.</p
